betterquesting:10.desc:8:
There are two things you must always remember when breeding anything:

- [note]Parents must be at least 80% mature§r[/note] in order to cross-breed, regardless of it's ability to keep growing.
- [note]Offsprings cannot appear without meeting all their growth requirements.[/note]

When breeding, the resulting stats are based on the rounded-down average of the §oparticipating§r parents' stats plus or minus a random value.

The range of this random value depends on 2 factors: The number of parents and the amount of fertilizer stored within them.

- Early on, breeding with multiple parents is the only way to attempt to improve your stats, but it's very slow.
- Applying fertilizer widen the range of values for multi-parent breeding and stabilizes stats during simple propagation.
- Using a Crop Manager to apply fertilizer allows you to rapidly improve the stats of your crops.

Multiple parent:
- 0 to 49 fertilizer: -1 -> +1 (higher chance for -1 and 1)
- 50-100 fertilizer: -2 -> +2
- 101+ fertilizer: 0 -> +4 (40% chance for 0)

Single parent:
- 0-49 fertilizer: -1 -> 0 (higher chance for 0)
- 50-100 fertilizer: no variation
- 100+ fertilizer: 0 -> +4 (40% chance for 0)

When breeding crops, there is a 50% chance for the offspring to be of the same species as one of the parents. When this happens, all the parents matching the species of the offspring are used to compute the rounded-down average.

There are 2 ways to obtain new species: Random Mutations and Deterministic Mutations.

Most crops have access to something called Mutation Pools. These pools are like a set of tags associated with each crop. When breeding, if of the parents some share one or more mutation pools, a Random mutation may occur. The resulting offspring will always be another species tagged with one of those shared pools.

[note]Once you've obtained your first 31/31/31 seed, it can be helpful to use these random pool mutations to collect many different types of crops.[/note]

Deterministic breeding is similar to how bees work, where you must bring the right species together. Some situations require more than two parents, and all parents must be adjacent to the double crop stick. During the early stages, you can often emulate deterministic breeding by tailoring the soil, sub-soil and environment of a double cropstick to control the outcome of a random mutation. This process is usually much slower than deterministic mutations, and might require a lot of baby sitting if the crop you wan\u0027t can be singled out/

[note]Deterministic Mutations always take priority over Random Mutations.§r[/note]

[note]Advanced crops (§5MV§r and above materials) will require the breeding machine.[/note]
